summary: Bolt found shown by Milne and declared to have been turned from the inside: supports a locked-room appearance.
Clock on mantel was stopped; later noted that the mechanism had stopped at 10:17. "I read later that the mechanism had stopped at 10:17; the note was dry and precise..."
Lena Harrow discovered at her desk with a heavy brass letter-opener driven into her chest; ribs bent faintly around the haft. "Set deep into Lena's chest was a heavy brass letter-opener..."

A bloodied handkerchief was clenched in Lena's hand; the handkerchief's initials were not listed on the housekeeper's slip. "The handkerchief's initials were not listed on the slip — they were simply noted as present — and that absence kept the name inside the cloth like a secret."

An improvised pulley anchor (short cord and loop of metal) was found hidden in the ivy on the exterior sill. "On the outer sill, tucked into the ivy... I found a short length of cord and a little loop of metal serving as a makeshift anchor."

A thin smear of oil was present along the haft of the letter-opener, suggestive of someone who handled machinery rather than paper. "there was, however, a thin smear of oil along the wood, the kind left by someone whose hands had been working on machinery rather than on paper."
A faint crescent of cigar ash was present on the sill; the narrator notes it did not match Lena Harrow's habits. "the faint crescent of cigar ash on the sill that did not match Lena's habits"
Narrator (August Crowe) entered the library where Inspector Milne had his hand on the bolt; the scene of discovery unfolded: the dead woman, the clock, the desk, and the hidden pulley anchor.
A page in Lena's folio has been torn cleanly away. "One page had been torn cleanly away."

A fresh smear of oil was found near the sill at the folio's edge, running to where a missing sheet had been. "I ran a fingertip along the paper where the missing sheet had once lain and found, near the sill, a fresh smear of oil that caught the light..."

A neat crescent of cigar ash sat in the kitchen ashtray on the sill; present but not conclusively linked to any named person in the room. "On the sill sat the kitchen ashtray, a neat crescent of cigar ash in it."

Henry gave a verbal alibi claiming he was in the smoking-room all evening and denied going near the library after nine; Milne made a note. "I watched him while Milne made a note and pretended not to."
Mary was shown the folio and stiffened, describing Lena's lists of names and times. "When I showed her the folio she stiffened... 'Lena kept lists,' Mary said."

Oliver admitted a recent argument about pay but claimed to have been at the greenhouse most of the day; he later left to speak to the men. "We had words about pay the week before... I was at the greenhouse most of the day — ask the men."

After questioning, Oliver left to speak to the men; Mary lingered by the door; Henry left toward the study. "Oliver left to speak to the men. Mary hovered by the door... Henry lit nothing but impatience and left in a direction that suggested a study."
Household interrogation: Crowe questioned Henry, Mary and Oliver in the library; each offered an alibi or account and left or stayed as the scene ended.
No measured dimensions or forensic photographs exist for the outer sill; absence of such records noted by investigator.
Crowe threaded a spare cord through the loop and tied it to the heft of the letter-opener as a weight, preparing an experiment.
Crowe performed a timed experiment: from sash to thrust to withdrawal and final pull the operation took less than a minute.
On a second trial Crowe let the opener bite into a pad of cloth simulating flesh; the oil on the haft smeared on the cloth.
Oliver interrupted the experiment: he grabbed Crowe's wrist, smelled of earth and tobacco, and began to wind the cord away as if to hide the device.
Daylight demonstration: Crowe reenacted the pulley-and-opener mechanism; Milne timed the action and reported 'Less than a minute.' The oil on the opener matched the smear by the folio.

Henry confessed on the record: he admitted going to Lena's window, fixing the loop in the ivy, knotting the cord, using the opener as weight and blade, removing a folio page, and pulling the sash neat again.
